issue_context.title: PIDPressure incorrect when system thread number exceeds 65538
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

Condition PIDPressure is not set to true when the system thread number exceeds 65538 even it's reaching the limit.

### What did you expect to happen?

Condition PIDPressure is set to true correctly

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

See cause below

### Anything else we need to know?

The bug is due to [using linux syscall](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/712745cb6755b3a28ca12292b30d138d5f737aa6/pkg/kubelet/stats/pidlimit/pidlimit_linux.go#L43) `sysinfo`, which truncates any process number greater than 65538 because of type conversion.

See kernel code [here](https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/latest/source/kernel/sys.c#L2571). Reading it from `/proc/loadavg` should be working.

### Kubernetes version

v1.23.1

### Cloud provider

<details>
NA
</details>


### OS version

<details>

```console
# On Linux:
$ uname -a
5.10.46
```

</details>

review_comments: If opening `/proc/loadavg` fails, won't this bear a risk of giving an erroneous reading?

Yes, however it doesn't make thing worse compared to previous code. 

Another possibility is that /proc/loadavg might be open and read successfully, but the content has been changed in format so the functions returns an error. 

I might be too conservative to keep the sysinfo code here.

I think it makes sense to keep it... at least for compatibility with older kernels?
I guess it's not easy to add a test with 65k+ processes to show the benefits of this patch?
/ok-to-test
Maybe we can start a pod that creates 65k+ tasks (on Linux, POSIX threads implemented as kernel tasks consume a PID each)? It's definitely possible to make that container image.
I made a tool that might help with this testing: https://github.com/sftim/manytasks

rust XD
@sftim looks good, however not sure if that fits our e2e testing... at least for local tinkering for sure it helps
let's have an e2e test for this functionality so we can make sure to catch potential issues with the format change.

There is an e2e test for pid eviction https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8a259641532d12f730d0fc6b237d36206d405e52/test/e2e_node/eviction_test.go#L448. I think it should be able to catch the format change.
can we leave a comment here on why we prefer to use /proc/loadavg as opposed to `Sysinfo`, i.e. link to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/107107?
